title: Company Peak Week: Orientation & Ask Brief
content:
Purpose:
This is the working brief for 'Peak Week' — a condensed company-wide set of short syncs, demo blocks, and leadership asks we want to run the week of May 4. Objective is to align teams on top-3 company priorities for H2, collect concise roll-up asks from each org, and land commitments for cross-functional initiatives (dedicated capacity rollouts, Private onboarding pilot, Optimize beta ramp).

Scope & constraints:
- 60–90 minute company orientation + a series of 30 min deep-dive breakouts (product, eng, go-to-market).
- Keep slide count for orientation <= 12; each breakout gets 6 slides max.
- Avoid heavy demos in orientation — demos belong in breakouts.
- Must produce a one-page rollup doc with: top-3 asks, owners, deadlines.
- Budget/time: avoid adding cross-org workshops beyond 2 hours per lead during the week.

High-level agenda (orientation):
1) 10m — Opening: quick context and H2 framing (CEO)
2) 12m — Performance snapshot + where we missed/overachieved on Q1 goals (Finance/Product)
3) 12m — Top platform bets & expected customer impact (Product/Eng lead)
4) 10m — Reliability/operational health ask (SRE lead + one concrete SLA ask)
5) 10m — GTM & Expansion asks (Growth/Sales)
6) 6m — How teams should use the week (templates + required deliverables)
7) 10m — Q&A + closing commitments

Breakouts (30m each):
- Hosted API roadmap + migration ask (product-hosted-api)
- Dedicated capacity capacity planning & commits (product-dedicated)
- Private deployment pilot checklist and security reviews (product-private)
- Observability and Rollouts: action items for Console (product-console-and-rollouts)
- Optimize: cost-savings playbook and pilot cohorts (product-optimize)
- Quick ops sync: deployments, region capacity, and incident playbook updates (eng-infrastructure/eng-sre)

Deliverables (end of Peak Week):
- One-pager rolling asks (CSV + consolidated doc) — owners + target dates.
- Updated OKR backlog entries for any committed asks (format: OKR / initiative / owner / due).
- Short recording + 3-min highlights clip for late viewers.

Leader asks (template we will collect from each org):
- 1 sentence ask (what you need from other teams)
- Rationale and impact (2–3 bullets)
- Owner (name + email) and an escalation contact
- Expected duration and deadline
- Required resources (people / infra / budget)

Pulling asks: timeline and owners
- 2026-03-10: Ask leads notified (done)
- 2026-03-20: Draft asks due (owner: Aisha Patel) — ask submitted to drive folder
- 2026-03-27: Consolidation + editing pass (owner: Miguel Torres)
- 2026-04-03: Leadership review & explicit approvals required (CEO + CTO)

Comms plan (pre, during, post):
- Pre (2 weeks out): short teaser email, one-pager summary for leads, calendar hold with breakout selection links. Slack channel #peak-week for real-time coordination.
- During: live Slack coverage + real-time notes in shared doc. Each breakout has one scribe.
- Post: rollup + recording + 3 action items per team pushed into Jira/Linear within 48 hours.

Logistics & owners (working list):
- Main orientation host: Jordan Kim (slides and script)
- Slide deck editor: Simone Laurent (style + final deck)
- Breakout scheduling: Evan Brooks (calendar + polls)
- Video + recording: Ops media (contracted) — confirm by 3/22
- Scribes: each breakout lead to assign (name in roster by 3/20)

Draft deck structure (orientation):
- Title slide (1)
- Why H2 matters — 2 slides (metrics + customer vignettes)
- Platform bets (3 slides)
- Ops & reliability ask (1 slide)
- GTM focus and early signals (1 slide)
- The asks template + next steps (1 slide)

Risk register (quick):
- Overloaded leaders: some teams already in release freeze. Mitigation: accept asynchronous asks and short prerecorded 2 min updates.
- Ask pile gets too long: enforce 1-sentence ask rule and triage to 'must have' vs 'nice to have'.
- Missing data to justify asks: product/finance to provide a data dump template (owner: Miguel).

Open questions / TBDs:
- Do we want a 'customer panel' slot? Pros: tangible impact. Con: schedule complexity. (Decision by 3/17)
- Should we require each team to attach a mini-eval or metric to any ask that affects inference economics? (Product + Research to weigh in.)
- Who signs off on committed infra spend > $50k? (Finance + CTO)

Quick templates (copy into forms):
- Ask title: one line
- Impact (quantifiable if possible): 1–2 bullets
- Dependencies: which teams, infra, compliance items
- Acceptable compromise: what we can accept if full ask can't be met

Notes to self / working scraps:
- Keep orientation under 75 mins — people lose focus.
- Consider a 2-day asynchronous window for EMEA timezones (recorded + short live reprise).
- We should reuse the OKR rollout checklist from Q4 (Confluence id above).

Next steps (immediate):
- 2026-03-10: send out formal 'asks' template (owner: Aisha) — DONE (note: check responses folder)
- 2026-03-20: chase teams that haven't filled the template (owner: Evan)
- 2026-03-22: confirm recording vendor + tech check (owner: Simone)
- 2026-03-27: first consolidation draft shared for leadership comments (owner: Miguel)

Appendix: links + references
- Peak week working folder: drive://shared/peak-week-2026 (placeholder)
- Past references: Q4 orientation playbook, exec-brief archive, incident-runbook-updates
- Related tickets: ENG-1123 (capacity forecast), FIN-203 (budget guardrail)

-- end --

(Stylistic note: keep this doc as the canonical working brief; when finalizing, copy content into the formal playbook template and create a slide deck in the 'presentation' folder.)
